answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then randomly select among eligible agents and slash the stake when independently verified output proves fraudulent. Creating a thousand sybils no longer gives an attacker free influence: every identity must tie up capital, and cheating risks losing it. The oasis of honest participation is protected not by a cipher or a voyage of trust, but by making each attempted fake costly and punishable.
